items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names are clear and public methods have doc comments. But no field in `durabilityState` is documented, the new batch fields (`commitApplyStart`, `durableHandled`, etc.) have no comments, and the retention/trim logic and the 1ns duration clamp in `onBatchDurable` are unexplained.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: The durable/closed/firstErr/seq checks are copied four times: in each wait loop and again in each `ctx.Done` branch, and similar logic appears in `DurabilityNotify`. `onBatchDurable` is long (~80 lines). The hook lives in db.go `applyInternal` instead of commit.go as the conventions ask.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Magic constants (`maxNotifySubs = 4096`, `maxRetainedJobs = 10000`). Job IDs come from `d.newJobID()`, which flush/compaction also use, so unused IDs in that range report "expired" instead of "unknown" (hidden test fails). Job IDs are 0 when no listener is set, so `WaitForJobDurability` cannot work then.

items.name: Commit path and public types remain backward compatible
items.name_zh: 提交路径与公共类型保持向后兼容
items.evidence: Every NoSyncWait sync commit now starts a goroutine (`go func(b *Batch){ b.fsyncWait.Wait() ...}`), even with no listener. `applyInternal` now sets `batch.db = d`, changing what that field means. `MakeLoggingEventListener` logs every sync commit, so an existing test had to set `lel.BatchDurable = nil`.
